es.summary: Daño tisular causado por la interrupción del flujo sanguíneo que priva al tejido de oxígeno y nutrientes.
key_points: La isquemia produce necrosis celular si la perfusión no se restablece en minutos a horas.
Factores como presión prolongada, inmovilidad y enfermedad vascular aumentan el riesgo.
Los signos iniciales pueden ser dolor, coloración pálida y pérdida de sensibilidad.
El diagnóstico se basa en la evaluación clínica y pruebas de perfusión (p. ej., doppler, angio‑CT).
El tratamiento incluye restaurar la circulación y prevenir complicaciones como úlceras por presión.

pathophysiology: Obstrucción de una arteria o compresión prolongada reduce el flujo sanguíneo.
Disminuye la entrega de oxígeno y glucosa, provocando daño de la membrana celular.
Se acumulan metabolitos tóxicos y se activa la inflamación, llevando a necrosis.
Si la isquemia persiste, se forma tejido necrótico y posible infección secundaria.
risk_factors: Presión externa sobre tejido (úlcera por presión, vendajes apretados).
signs_symptoms: Dolor localizado que empeora con la presión.
Pérdida de sensibilidad o entumecimiento en la zona afectada.
Edema leve y posible aparición de ampollas.
diagnostics: Inspección visual y palpación de color, temperatura y dolor.
Doppler arterial para evaluar flujo sanguíneo.
Angio‑CT o resonancia magnética si se sospecha compromiso profundo.
Laboratorio: lactato elevado (>2 mmol/L) indica hipoxia tisular.
treatment: Reposicionamiento frecuente para aliviar la presión.
Descompresión quirúrgica o trombólisis según causa vascular.
Oxígeno suplementario y control de glucemia.
Uso de apósitos hidrocoloidales o alginato para proteger la zona.
complications: Úlcera por presión de estadio III‑IV.
Necrosis extensa con pérdida de tejido.
nursing_care: Evaluar color, temperatura y dolor cada 2 h.
Reposicionar al paciente cada 2 h y usar superficies de alivio de presión.
Mantener la piel limpia y seca; aplicar apósitos adecuados.
Monitorizar signos vitales y lactato sérico.
Documentar cambios y comunicar al equipo médico.
patient_teaching: Importancia de cambiar de posición cada 2 h y usar almohadas de apoyo.
Mantener la piel hidratada y evitar ropa ajustada.
Reportar dolor nuevo o aumento de sensibilidad inmediatamente.
Seguir dieta equilibrada rica en proteínas para favorecer la cicatrización.

outcomes: Seguridad del paciente: sin eventos de caída o lesión durante la hospitalización.
Integridad física: mantener la integridad de la piel y tejidos blandos.

interventions.action: Mantener el área de trabajo libre de obstáculos y usar barandillas de cama.
Colocar al paciente en posición semisentado si presenta dificultad respiratoria.
interventions.rationale: Reduce el riesgo de aspiración y mejora la comodidad.

interventions.action: Revisar y asegurar que los dispositivos (catéteres, tubos) estén bien fijados.
interventions.rationale: Evita tirones y lesiones por desplazamiento.

interventions.action: Realizar educación sobre la importancia de solicitar ayuda antes de levantarse.
interventions.rationale: Fomenta conductas seguras y reduce intentos de movilización sin asistencia.

en.summary: Tissue damage caused by interruption of blood flow that deprives tissue of oxygen and nutrients.
key_points: Ischemia produces cellular necrosis if perfusion is not restored within minutes to hours.
Factors such as prolonged pressure, immobility and vascular disease increase risk.
Initial signs may be pain, pallor and loss of sensation.
Diagnosis is based on clinical assessment and perfusion tests (e.g., Doppler, angio‑CT).
Treatment includes restoring circulation and preventing complications such as pressure ulcers.

pathophysiology: Arterial obstruction or prolonged compression reduces blood flow.
Decreases delivery of oxygen and glucose, causing cellular membrane damage.
Toxic metabolites accumulate and inflammation is activated, leading to necrosis.
If ischemia persists, necrotic tissue forms and secondary infection may occur.
risk_factors: External pressure on tissue (pressure ulcer, tight dressings).
signs_symptoms: Loss of sensation or numbness in affected area.
Mild edema and possible blister formation.
diagnostics: Visual inspection and palpation of color, temperature and pain.
Arterial Doppler to assess blood flow.
Angio‑CT or MRI if deep involvement suspected.
Laboratory: elevated lactate (>2 mmol/L) indicates tissue hypoxia.
treatment: Surgical decompression or thrombolysis depending on vascular cause.
Use hydrocolloid or alginate dressings to protect the area.
nursing_care: Assess color, temperature and pain every 2 h.
Reposition patient every 2 h and use pressure‑relieving surfaces.
Keep skin clean and dry; apply appropriate dressings.
Monitor vital signs and serum lactate.
Document changes and communicate with medical team.
patient_teaching: Importance of changing position every 2 h and using supportive pillows.
Keep skin hydrated and avoid tight clothing.
Report new pain or increased sensitivity immediately.
Follow a balanced diet rich in protein to promote healing.

outcomes: Patient safety: no falls or injuries during hospitalization.
Physical integrity: maintain skin and soft tissue integrity.

interventions.action: Keep the work area free of obstacles and use bed rails.
Place patient in semi‑upright position if they have respiratory difficulty.
interventions.rationale: Reduces aspiration risk and improves comfort.

interventions.action: Check and secure devices (catheters, tubes) are properly fastened.
interventions.rationale: Prevents pulls and injuries from displacement.

interventions.action: Educate on the importance of asking for help before standing.
interventions.rationale: Encourages safe behaviors and reduces attempts to mobilize without assistance.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: In thrombosis, an obstructive process prevents blood flow to regions of the brain.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Common risk factors for development of a pressure injury include advanced age, immobility, friction, shear, poor nutrition, excessive moisture and incontinence, altered level of consciousness, poor perfusion, certain skin infections, and comorbid conditions.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: The tolerance of soft tissue for pressure and shear may also be affected by microclimate (e.g., skin temperature, moisture), nutrition, perfusion, comorbidities, and condition of the soft tissue.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: It may involve intact or nonintact skin with possible epidermal separation that reveals a dark wound bed or blood-filled blister.

sections.diagnostics.0.quote: Noticeable changes in sensation, temperature, or firmness may precede visual changes.

sections.treatment.0.quote: Typically, the unofficial rule of turning and repositioning every two hours is implemented for all patients at risk for skin breakdown; although this is a general rule, some patients require more frequent turns (or fewer manual turns if they are able to reposition themselves).
